# Welcome {.unnumbered}

Learn to turn dimensions and drawings into clear, checkable 3D geometry.

These practicals accompany **Ship Geometry** for Naval Architecture students at **FESB, University of Split**. Start with a simple pontoon to learn Rhino, reconstruct and check a hull surface, model a keel fin with a ballast bulb, transfer a hull into Maxsurf, produce a lines plan and lay out a boat interior in Rhino. No previous CAD experience is assumed for the first exercise.

## How to work through a practical

Keep the exercise next to Rhino. Read one short stage, perform it, then stop at its **checkpoint** to inspect the result. Read Rhino's command prompt before the next click. Save the named checkpoints so you can recover a sound earlier model instead of starting over.

Commands appear as `_Box` or `_Move`. Type the command and press Enter; the underscore requests the English name in a translated Rhino interface. Coordinates such as `w2,0,0` are **world coordinates** in metres. Each exercise explains the inputs rather than requiring you to recognise every toolbar icon.

::: {.callout-note title="One coordinate convention throughout"}
**X forward · Y to port · Z upward · Centreplane Y = 0.**

Top shows XY, Front shows the XZ profile, and Right shows the YZ body plan. “Front” is Rhino's world-view name; it does not mean the ship's bow view.
:::

## What you need

Use Rhino 8 for Exercises 1–3 and 5–7. Exercise 4 also requires Maxsurf Modeler. On macOS, use the named Rhino commands when panels or shortcuts differ. No plugins, Grasshopper, Git or Python are needed by students. A wheel mouse is helpful.

Input files for Exercises 2 and 3 are linked on their pages. Exercises 5–7 use the completed hull model from Exercise 2. Read the [Maxsurf introduction](maxsurf-introduction.qmd) before Exercise 4, which transfers the hull from Exercise 2 into Maxsurf. The course text and practice data do not depend on playing a video. External documentation and video links need internet access; their original pages are linked as fallbacks.

## Finding information

Use the sidebar to change exercises, the page contents to jump between stages, and search to find a command. Browser printing provides a paper copy of the current lesson; video links remain in the printed text. The [reference library](resources.qmd) groups the official documentation, media credits and practice-data details.

The exercises prioritise **measured dimensions, organised construction and explicit checks** over an attractive screenshot. A convincing shaded view alone does not establish that a model is accurate, fair or watertight.
